title: Project configuration — software-analysis capability
description: Formal shape of the project's `.pkit/capabilities/software-analysis/project/config.yaml`: the settings of the capability a project chooses. One today, `numbering.freed-by` (DEC-001 point 3): the commits by which the default branch lost artefacts whose numbers are free again. Whether each is a commit of the default branch's history here, and frees a number, the stamp (`pkit analysis new`) and the number check (`pkit analysis check-numbers`) judge, since each reads git; not this schema. Document-shaped schema: the file IS the resource (no top-level id collection). Companion per COR-018.

binds_to.description: Repo-relative globs matching the adopter-data files this schema validates (COR-023 fallback binding). Present on the capability-side carrier; absent from a project's file.

numbering.description: How use cases and journeys are numbered (DEC-001 point 3).

freed-by.description: The commits by which the default branch lost artefacts nothing still relies on, whose numbers are free again: a number the default branch's history gave only files one of them deleted — not renamed — and by which the default branch lost them last is no longer counted. Nothing else frees a number through the stamp: a file any other commit removed still holds its number, and so does a file the working tree or the default branch holds.

commit-id.description: A commit, by its full hexadecimal id in lower case — 40 digits, or 64 in a SHA-256 repository: an abbreviation can come to name two commits as history grows. Quoted in YAML, as digits alone can read as a number.
